title: Orchestrator circuit breaker and livepatch for onprem Helm reconcile stalls
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
A high-severity customer escalation: several VPC/on‑prem tenants observed prolonged Helm/operator reconciliation stalls during a weekend rolling upgrade. Symptoms were controller loops stuck in backoff for specific namespaces, manifests not progressing, and an increase in request 5xx errors for model serving endpoints. Root cause analysis indicates a short-lived combination of: (1) certificate rotation timing that triggered mutating webhook restarts, (2) operator leader-election flapping across control-plane replicas, and (3) a KV cache corruption scenario where a partially-applied upgrade left a stale prefix in the on‑disk cache leading to deserialization errors during CR reconciliation.

Why this is customer-impacting:
- Tenants experienced failed in-place upgrades and lost automated retries, requiring manual operator restarts.
- For Dedicated and Private customers this caused SLA violations and escalations to support and engineering.

Proposed short-term mitigation (hotfix):
1) Operator-level upgrade circuit breaker: implement a toggle (config + API) that detects reconciliation error rate and flips operator into 'safe-mode' where it pauses non-essential hooks, inhibits in-place Helm post-upgrade hooks, and forces lightweight state snapshot + upload to S3/K8s secret.
2) Livepatch sidecar that can be executed without full operator restart: runs a transactional KV-cache repair routine (validate, reconstruct missing keys from CR history, rotate corrupt entries) and rehydrates in-memory caches.
3) Clearer preflight check for Helm upgrades: validate webhook cert expiry windows and node kubelet transient states before starting phased rollout.
4) Automated canary rollout by namespace with circuit-break thresholds and automatic rollback to previous Helm revision on repeated reconcile failures.

Trade-offs considered:
- Pausing reconciliation reduces blast radius but increases time-to-repair. Chosen threshold tuned conservatively to favor tenant availability (pause after 6 transient reconciles over 10m).
- Snapshot-and-pause requires secure short-term storage; will use existing tenant object-store integration with encryption-at-rest (no new infra).
- Livepatch avoids cold restart but increases code surface in operator; we limit its capabilities to deterministic KV fixes and extensive logging + no-op dry-run mode.

Implementation plan (short-term):
- Week-of hotfix branch: operator/cmd: add circuit-breaker FSM (feature flag off by default), livepatch sidecar binary, and a Helm preflight plugin.
- Add end-to-end test harness using the CI k3s cluster: simulate webhook rotation + leader-election flapping + partial manifest application and validate circuit-breaker transitions and livepatch success.
- Metrics/alerts: new Prometheus metrics (operator_reconcile_errors_total, operator_circuit_breaker_state, kv_livepatch_runs_total) and Grafana dashboard tile for onprem rollouts.
- Customer communication: draft incident summary + recommended manual remediation steps for tenants already affected.

Longer-term work (follow-ups):
- Harden leader-election to prefer control-plane stable nodes via a weights table and backoff jitter tuning.
- Rework KV cache on-disk format to be atomic-write friendly and include checksums + versioned backups.
- Integrate with Console to provide per-tenant upgrade health view and one-click rollback.

Runbook / Manual remediation steps (for Support):
- Verify operator pod logs for "kv-deserialize-error" and record failing CRs.
- If circuit-breaker is available, set operator config to safe-mode to prevent repeated retries: kubectl patch configmap operator-config --patch '{"data":{"circuit_breaker":"on"}}'.
- Run livepatch sidecar: kubectl run kv-livepatch --image=redwood/operator-livepatch:hotfix-2025.02 --namespace redwood-ops --restart=Never --command -- /bin/livepatch repair --tenant <TENANT>
